title: Multiplicativity of regularized determinants
statement: For specified admissible elliptic operators and a fixed regularization, determine the defect \(\log\det(AB)-\log\det A-\log\det B\), and conditions under which it vanishes. The operator order, spectral cuts, commutativity, and treatment of kernels must be fixed.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the multiplicative anomaly and its local-residue description are established in the settings treated by \citet{kontsevichvishik1994geometry}. Unqualified multiplicativity is false; this occurrence reuses the earlier precise problem.

title: Odd-moduli integration and the higher-genus RNS measure
statement: For super Riemann surfaces of a fixed genus and spin parity, determine the odd-moduli pushforward of the RNS measure on any specified projection domain, its modular transformation, and its degeneration behavior. Separately determine whether a global holomorphic projection to reduced spin moduli exists.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the global-projection premise is obstructed for \(g\geq5\) by Donagi--Witten and for both parity components in every \(g\geq3\) by the theorem stated in the September 2026 Correa--Donagi--Noja preprint. Local odd integration remains meaningful. The 2025 genus-three analysis proves a three-term form but leaves its exact coefficient values conjectural and its numerical extraction without a rigorous error bound. Thus that coefficient determination remains a precise partial remainder; no general unsolved global projection is asserted.

title: Which lattice theta sums have the required modular transformation?
statement: For a positive-definite lattice, determine the modular transformation of its theta series, specifying the modular group and scalar, multiplier, or vector-valued representation. The seminar asks whether the desired full-group scalar transformation forces even unimodularity.
status: As of 12 November 2026, Poisson summation gives the precise dual-lattice transformation, and even unimodular lattices supply the full modular-group scalar form in the stated convention. Theta series of other integral lattices remain modular for suitable subgroups or vector-valued representations, so the unrestricted only-if assertion is false. This is a settled clarification, not a new open problem.

title: A common linear complex structure for real codimension-two arrangements
statement: Given real codimension-two linear subspaces \(L_i\subset\mathbb R^{2m}\), decide whether there is a real linear operator \(J\) with \(J^2=-I\) and \(J(L_i)=L_i\) for every \(i\). A 2-arrangement also imposes even-codimension intersection conditions; these are additional hypotheses, not an automatic consequence of the individual codimensions.
status: As of 12 November 2026, the proposed automatic complexification is false. For pairwise transverse planes in \(\mathbb R^4\), \citet[Theorems 1 and 3]{batzies2007planes} gives simultaneous-conjugacy and four-plane criteria. The chapter rederives a bounded linear-algebra formulation as an annotation to known work, with no new research claim and no inference that a higher-dimensional classification is an open problem. Topological equivalence is not settled by the linear criterion.

title: Polynomial quotients of the affine type-A Hecke algebra
statement: For \(q\ne0\), identify the universal quotient of the affine type-A Hecke algebra by \(p(X_n)=0\), where \(p\) is monic of degree \(r\) with nonzero constant term, and determine its dimension and a basis; the notebook singles out \(p(z)=z^2-1\).
status: As of 12 November 2026, this is the cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type \(G(r,1,n)\), of dimension \(r^n n!\); \(r=2\) yields type B. The Ariki--Koike basis theorem holds without semisimplicity, as read in \citet[\S2, (2.2)]{mathas2004matrix}. The universal quotient target answers the precise notebook reading adopted here; it is not a claim of an evaluation into the original finite type-A algebra for every polynomial.
